The frozen leading-shift extremizer sentence (line 54) omitted lambda>0: for lambda=0 and K>1 every allocation attains both extrema, so uniqueness is false on the literal critical-window range. The replacement gives both cases and makes finite-cutoff moment uniform integrability explicit. Perimeter is 2n using the continuous convention for a degenerate segment. The pair area formula and the absolutely summable Fourier expansion of |sin| give exactly the positive quadratic sum, including its diagonal 1/pi in the expectation. Orthogonality gives the means epsilon_n eta_m; real multivariate Lindeberg applies to the bounded centered coordinates with limiting covariance (1/2)I. The centered sixth-moment expansion has at most O(n³) surviving terms before normalization, uniform in mode; thus squared-cutoff uniform integrability and a summable uniform L² tail follow. The Euler sine product has numerator normalization 2/pi and continuations as stated; partial fractions in the central squared weights give 1/4-2/pi². After dividing the Laplace transforms by the same positive baseline, the modes have separate rational poles -1/c_m with residues -lambda|eta_m|²/c_m; the inverse identifies exactly those products, or the powers for fixed positive lambda. Direct mean/cross/noise bounds give L¹ convergence above the window. The frozen finite checker was inspected, not rerun; its Monte Carlo and truncation diagnostics do not establish the inverse or limiting theorem.
